analysis.research_question_and_background: Molecular syndromic panels such as the BioFire FilmArray Gastrointestinal Panel have been widely adopted for gastrointestinal illness diagnosis due to their fast turnaround times and broad pathogen coverage, but recent data have suggested significant norovirus false-positive results associated with this panel.
analysis.study_design_and_population: We examined the prevalence of BF-GIP norovirus false positives across four hospitals from December 2024 to June 2025.
analysis.methods: Deep sequencing of BF-GIP pouches (n = 42) confirmed the Noro-1 assay as the primary source of off-target amplification, identifying 78 off-target species-predominantly commensal stool bacteria-compared to only two species for the Noro-2 assay.
analysis.main_results: Among 185 BF-GIP norovirus-positive results confirmed with the BD MAX Enteric Viral Panel, the false discovery rate ranged from 31% to 74% across sites, with the highest rate seen at a specialized cancer care hospital.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: These findings highlight the high false discovery rate of the Noro-1 assay, identify bacterial species involved in mispriming, and demonstrate the need to redesign this assay to ensure reliable testing and improved patient care.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The identification of discrete loci with partial primer overlap, combined with the repeatedly high false discovery rate reported across multiple studies, creates a clinical imperative to redesign this assay and highlights the ongoing need for rigorous post-market surveillance.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence strength is high due to the large sample size and confirmatory testing, though the study was limited to four hospitals and may not represent all clinical settings.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the high false-positive rate of norovirus detection on the BioFire FilmArray Gastrointestinal Panel (BF-GIP), which led to a Class II recall in 2024. Across four hospitals, the false discovery rate ranged from 31% to 74%, with the highest rate at a specialized cancer care hospital. Deep sequencing of BF-GIP pouches identified 78 bacterial species as off-target amplification sources, primarily from the Noro-1 assay. The findings confirm mispriming with gut microbiota as the cause, with partial primer complementarity and amplicon Tm values supporting this mechanism. The study underscores the need to redesign the Noro-1 assay and emphasizes the importance of post-market surveillance for molecular diagnostic panels.

It highlights FMT's potential therapeutic mechanisms, including microbiota engraftment, mucosal barrier repair, and immune modulation. While existing evidence suggests FMT may be effective and safe, particularly in immunocompromised patients, current studies are limited to case reports and small series. The review emphasizes the need for larger randomized controlled trials and standardized protocols to validate FMT's clinical value and guide its implementation.

This method offers a cost-effective alternative to eukaryotic systems, potentially advancing diagnostic assay development for norovirus gastroenteritis.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Human norovirus (HNV) causes up to 700 million infections and 200,000 deaths annually, primarily affecting young children in low-resource settings, yet no licensed vaccines or anti-viral therapies exist. The mechanisms underlying protective immunity to HNV remain poorly defined, posing a major barrier to rational vaccine design.
analysis.study_design_and_population: We used a panel of genetically and pharmacologically modified mice to investigate the correlates and cellular determinants of protection to murine norovirus (MNV) infection, which serves as a genetically tractable model for HNV.
analysis.methods: We employed genetically and pharmacologically modified mice to investigate the correlates and cellular determinants of protection to MNV infection, focusing on T cell-dependent IgA and CD8+ T cells.
analysis.main_results: T cell-dependent IgA is necessary to control MNV replication in the small intestine, whereas CD8+ T cells are dispensable; IgA plasma cells mediate protection from re-infection, and dimeric IgA, but not monomeric, is sufficient to confer complete protection against MNV infection.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: Our work shows that mucosal IgA is central to controlling norovirus infection in a murine model, providing important insights for rational vaccine design and HNV immunotherapeutics.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings highlight the critical role of mucosal IgA in norovirus protection, informing the development of effective vaccines and immunotherapeutics that target mucosal immunity rather than systemic responses.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study was conducted in a murine model, which may not fully recapitulate human norovirus infection; however, the evidence strength is high due to the rigorous use of genetically and pharmacologically modified mice to establish causal relationships.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the mechanisms of protective immunity against norovirus using a murine model. The researchers found that T cell-dependent IgA is necessary to control norovirus replication in the small intestine, while CD8+ T cells are dispensable. Dimeric IgA, but not monomeric, is sufficient to confer complete protection against infection. In contrast, systemic vaccination with the viral capsid protein fails to protect mice, mirroring human vaccine failures. These findings demonstrate that mucosal IgA is central to controlling norovirus infection and provide critical insights for designing effective vaccines and immunotherapeutics that target mucosal immunity.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Human noroviruses (HuNoVs) are a leading cause of acute gastroenteritis worldwide, yet no effective antiviral therapeutics are currently available. Although environmentally induced capsid conformational changes associated with infectivity have been reported in murine noroviruses (MNVs), comparable conformational switching has not been demonstrated in HuNoVs.
analysis.study_design_and_population: In this study, we generated HuNoV GII.3 virus-like particles (VLPs) using a baculovirus expression system and identified two distinct T = 3 particle populations coexisting within VLP preparations derived from a single strain through cryo-electron microscopy single-particle analysis.
analysis.methods: Comparative structural analysis revealed that these two T = 3 capsid conformations correspond to the resting and rising states of the protruding (P) domain. Rearrangement of the P domain alters intermolecular interactions between adjacent capsid subunits, resulting in distinct capsid surface architectures.
analysis.main_results: In the resting state, intermolecular contacts were mediated predominantly by the P2 subdomain, with limited contribution from the P1 subdomain. In contrast, the rising state exhibited a shift toward an alternative interaction interface primarily involving the P1 subdomain. The alteration of the capsid surface accompanying this conformational switching can influence biologically relevant intermolecular interactions with viral hosts and antibodies as demonstrated in murine norovirus.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: These findings demonstrate previously unrecognized structural polymorphism in the HuNoV capsid and provide evidence that conformational switching may occur in HuNoVs. Our results offer new insights into norovirus capsid dynamics and may inform future structure-based vaccine and antiviral drug development.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that conformational switching in the HuNoV capsid could influence interactions with viral hosts and antibodies, potentially informing the development of structure-based vaccines and antiviral drugs. This structural polymorphism may have implications for understanding norovirus infectivity and immune evasion mechanisms.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study was conducted using virus-like particles rather than infectious virions, which may not fully represent the natural state of the virus. However, the use of cryo-electron microscopy single-particle analysis provides high-resolution structural data, supporting a moderate assessment of evidence strength.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the conformational plasticity of the human norovirus GII.3 capsid by generating virus-like particles (VLPs) and analyzing them through cryo-electron microscopy. The researchers identified two distinct T = 3 capsid conformations corresponding to resting and rising states of the protruding (P) domain. In the resting state, intermolecular contacts were mediated primarily by the P2 subdomain, while the rising state involved an alternative interface with the P1 subdomain. This structural polymorphism demonstrates previously unrecognized conformational switching in HuNoVs, which may influence interactions with hosts and antibodies. The findings provide new insights into norovirus capsid dynamics and could inform future structure-based vaccine and antiviral drug development, addressing the need for effective therapeutics against this leading cause of acute gastroenteritis.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Norovirus is a leading cause of acute gastroenteritis (AGE) in the United States and is associated with substantial healthcare utilization, including risk of hospitalization. The extent to which underlying medical conditions contribute to this risk is not well understood.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This retrospective cohort study analyzed adults with incident medically attended all-cause AGE or cause-specified norovirus AGE episodes identified via International Classification of Diseases, Tenth Revision, Clinical Modification between July 1, 2022, and June 30, 2024 in Optum’s de-identified Clinformatics® Data Mart Database (Optum® CDM).
analysis.methods: Generalized estimating equations estimated adjusted risk ratios (aRRs) and confidence intervals (CIs) for acute hospitalization within three days of AGE diagnoses.
analysis.main_results: Of 1,705,514 all-cause AGE and 5,805 norovirus AGE cases, 11.3% and 44.6%, respectively, were hospitalized within three days of their episode. Hospitalization risk was higher for patients with cardiovascular disease (all-cause AGE aRR: 1.67 [95% CI, 1.64–1.69]; norovirus AGE aRR: 1.37 [1.22–1.54]), blood disorders, chronic respiratory disease, and chronic kidney disease.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: Underlying conditions, notably cardiovascular disease and ≥2 underlying conditions, significantly increased the risk of acute hospitalization, which was elevated among adults aged 18–64 years.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings highlight the importance of identifying underlying medical conditions, particularly cardiovascular disease and multiple comorbidities, in assessing hospitalization risk for norovirus gastroenteritis, which may inform targeted prevention and management strategies.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study relied on administrative claims data, which may have limitations in capturing clinical details and potential misclassification. However, the large sample size and robust statistical methods provide high confidence in the results.

analysis.summary_en: This retrospective cohort study investigated individual-level factors associated with acute hospitalization after medically attended acute gastroenteritis (AGE) and norovirus gastroenteritis in the United States from 2022 to 2024. Analyzing over 1.7 million all-cause AGE and 5,805 norovirus AGE cases, the study found that 11.3% and 44.6% of patients, respectively, were hospitalized within three days. Underlying conditions, particularly cardiovascular disease and the presence of two or more conditions, significantly increased hospitalization risk, with adjusted risk ratios ranging from 1.37 to 2.02. Notably, the relative risk was higher among adults aged 18–64 years compared to those 65 and older. These findings underscore the importance of considering comorbidities in assessing norovirus-related hospitalization risk, potentially guiding targeted clinical interventions and public health strategies.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Despite the considerable burden of diarrheal disease in Asia, etiology-specific patterns remain insufficiently characterized. This study aimed to provide a comprehensive assessment of the diarrheal disease burden across Asia from 1990 to 2023, focusing on the implications for travelers' diarrhea.
analysis.study_design_and_population: We estimated the burden of diarrheal disease in Asia, including Central, East, South, Southeast Asia, and High-income Asia Pacific, across 34 countries from 1990 to 2023 using the Global Burden of Diseases Study 2023.
analysis.methods: Disease burden was calculated using age-standardized disability-adjusted life year rates (ASDRs) per 100,000 population, with 95% uncertainty intervals (UIs). Additionally, we assessed the burden attributable to risk factors and calculated pathogen-specific estimates for 13 major etiologies.
analysis.main_results: From 1990 to 2023, ASDRs of diarrheal disease declined across Asia, with the largest decline in South Asia from 9124.29 (95% UI, 7594.46-11,673.82) per 100,000 population to 1216.90 (965.73-1633.55). Although norovirus was the leading etiology in High-income Asia Pacific, rotavirus remained dominant across all other Asian regions in 2023.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The heterogeneity in etiology-specific burden, age- and sex-related vulnerability, and associations with SDI across Asia underscores the need for destination-specific risk assessment and context-sensitive prevention strategies for travelers' diarrhea in Asia.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings inform targeted prevention strategies for travelers' diarrhea in Asia, highlighting the importance of considering regional variations in etiology and risk factors.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study relies on the Global Burden of Diseases Study 2023, which may have limitations in data quality and completeness for certain regions and time periods. The evidence strength is moderate due to the comprehensive nature of the data but potential biases in surveillance and reporting.

analysis.summary_en: This study assessed the burden of diarrheal disease in Asia from 1990 to 2023, focusing on implications for travelers' diarrhea. Using the Global Burden of Diseases Study 2023, researchers calculated age-standardized disability-adjusted life year rates (ASDRs) and pathogen-specific estimates across 34 countries. Results showed a significant decline in diarrheal disease burden, with rotavirus remaining dominant except in High-income Asia Pacific, where norovirus was the leading etiology. The burden was highest among children under 5 years and adults aged 95 years and older. Unsafe water sources were the leading risk factor, particularly in South Asia. The study emphasizes the need for region-specific risk assessments and prevention strategies for travelers' diarrhea in Asia.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Norovirus is a leading cause of acute gastroenteritis worldwide due to its high contagiousness, widespread transmission, and the lack of treatment or vaccine. In Senegal, no routine community-level monitoring is performed, and most available data concern other enteric viruses, leaving a gap in understanding norovirus circulation.
analysis.study_design_and_population: To assess the potential of wastewater surveillance as an early warning system, we analyzed the spatiotemporal circulation in Senegal of noroviruses using clinical and environmental data collected between 2020 and 2023, combining statistical and machine learning models, and comparing effective reproduction number R(t) estimates between genotypes and surveillance systems.
analysis.methods: Our data show that norovirus GII was the dominant genotype during the study period. Modeling data indicated more persistent circulation of norovirus GII than GI. Our study provides the first countrywide data on the application of wastewater-based epidemiology to monitor noroviruses across diverse geographic and demographic settings in Senegal.
analysis.main_results: Interestingly, peaks of viral load in environmental setting frequently preceded increases in reported clinical cases.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: Comparison of the effective reproduction number R(t) confirmed the descriptive data and highlighted a more persistent circulation for norovirus GII and a detection of R(t)'s increases in wastewater data prior to variation in clinical data, underscoring the usefulness of wastewater environmental surveillance as an early warning tool system for norovirus surveillance.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: Our data offer a proactive, cost-effective method to monitor public health trends and identify the presence of noroviruses within the population, offering an early warning system for community spread. The approach could be useful for the monitoring of other public health concerns in Senegal in the absence of routine clinical surveillance.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: In addition, a strong spatial heterogeneity in viral load was identified between wastewater collection sites, with high titers observed in several wastewater collection sites.

analysis.summary_en: This study conducted a 3-year wastewater-based epidemiology investigation of noroviruses in Senegal, aiming to evaluate the potential of wastewater surveillance as an early warning system. The research combined clinical and environmental data from 2020 to 2023, using statistical and machine learning models to compare effective reproduction numbers (R(t)) between genotypes and surveillance systems. The main results showed that norovirus GII was the dominant genotype, with peaks in viral load in the environmental setting often preceding increases in clinical cases. The authors interpreted these findings as evidence of the utility of wastewater surveillance for tracking norovirus circulation and detecting outbreaks before they are clinically apparent. The study highlights the importance of wastewater-based methods for monitoring noroviruses, especially in low-resource settings where clinical surveillance is limited. However, the authors noted strong spatial heterogeneity in viral load across collection sites, which may affect the generalizability of the findings. The study is significant for its countrywide application of wastewater-based epidemiology to monitor norovirus across diverse geographic and demographic settings in Senegal, offering a cost-effective early warning system for community spread. The evidence is moderate in strength due to the limitations in spatial uniformity and the potential for confounding factors.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The San Diego/Tijuana coastal region faces significant water quality issues due to untreated wastewater sources, necessitating a forecasting system for swimmer illness risk.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study developed the Pathogen Forecast Model (PFM) V1.0, which provides daily 5-day forecasts of swimmer illness risk along 30 km of shoreline in the San Diego/Tijuana region.
analysis.methods: PFM is based on a hydrodynamic model using forecasted waves, winds, offshore currents, and Tijuana River flow as inputs, with a modeled tracer concentration representing Norovirus decay.

analysis.study_design_and_population: This study optimized and evaluated a novel antifreeze–peracetic acid formulation (Af-PAA) for application on frozen foods, achieving disinfection performance at −40 °C. HuNoV GII.4[P31] propagated in zebrafish was inoculated onto frozen food samples.
analysis.methods: The formulation was optimized using four indicator microorganisms, with effective Af-PAA concentrations of 200 mg/L for Escherichia coli, 200 mg/L for Staphylococcus aureus, 500 mg/L for Candida albicans, and 2000 mg/L for Aspergillus niger. analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The optimized Af-PAA formulation provides a practical solution for disinfecting frozen foods, addressing a critical gap in food safety during cold chain storage and transportation.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study demonstrated high efficacy in controlled laboratory conditions, but further validation in real-world settings and with additional food matrices is needed to assess generalizability. analysis.summary_en: This study addressed the challenge of disinfecting frozen foods contaminated with human norovirus (HuNoV), a major foodborne pathogen. The optimized concentrations varied by food type and microorganism, demonstrating the formulation's adaptability. This novel approach offers a practical solution for microbial risk control in cold-chain foods, potentially enhancing food safety during storage and transportation.

The results indicate that Tulane virus readily aggregates in conditions typical of food and environmental systems, offering insights into norovirus adsorption and stability. However, the study was limited to in vitro experiments, which may not fully represent real-world scenarios. The findings have moderate scientific significance for understanding norovirus behavior in environmental matrices, but they do not directly inform public health interventions or policies.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Norovirus is the leading cause of acute gastroenteritis globally and causes significant morbidity, but it is not reportable to the public health system in most jurisdictions, making it challenging to detect and control local transmission.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This study was conducted in British Columbia, Canada, from January 10, 2021, to September 27, 2025, using wastewater samples from 12 municipal treatment plants and comparing them with norovirus-related hospital admissions and genogroup I (GI)-related emergency department visits.
analysis.methods: More than six thousand (n=6,167) wastewater samples were collected and pooled to generate a population-weighted average for the province, while norovirus hospital admissions and GI-related ED visits were extracted from the Discharge Abstract Database and the National Ambulatory Care Reporting System, respectively, and compared using time-lagged cross-correlation analyses.
analysis.main_results: Time-lagged cross-correlation analyses indicate significant positive correlation between unadjusted norovirus wastewater concentrations and norovirus hospitalizations (Spearman's ρ=0.69, p<0.01) and GI-related ED visits (Spearman's ρ=0.84, p<0.01), with wastewater leading hospitalizations by two weeks and aligned with ED visits.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings support the validity of using wastewater-based epidemiology for monitoring norovirus at the population-level and suggest that it may provide an early warning signal for severe norovirus activity requiring hospitalization, prompting a more timely response.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: Wastewater surveillance can serve as an early warning indicator for norovirus, enabling more timely public health responses and improving the detection and control of local transmission, particularly in jurisdictions where norovirus is not reportable.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence strength is high due to the large sample size and significant statistical correlations, though limitations may include potential confounding factors in wastewater sampling and clinical data collection.

analysis.summary_en: This study validates wastewater surveillance as an early warning indicator for norovirus in British Columbia, Canada, from 2021 to 2025. By analyzing over 6,000 wastewater samples and comparing them with clinical data, researchers found significant positive correlations between wastewater signals and hospitalizations (ρ=0.69, p<0.01) and emergency department visits (ρ=0.84, p<0.01), with wastewater leading hospitalizations by two weeks. The findings support wastewater-based epidemiology as a valuable tool for population-level norovirus monitoring, potentially enabling earlier public health interventions. This approach addresses the challenge of detecting norovirus in jurisdictions where it is not reportable, offering a non-invasive method for surveillance.

analysis.summary_en: This study quantified human-associated sewage markers (HF183 and PMMoV) and enteric viruses (NoVGII and HAdV) in paired water and air samples from three coastal sites in San Diego County, USA, including the Tijuana River, Imperial Beach, and La Jolla Shores. The authors concluded that coastal surf zones may serve as important interfaces for aerosolization of wastewater-associated microorganisms and proposed PMMoV as a conservative indicator of aerosolized human fecal viruses. analysis.research_question_and_background: Multiscale models for infectious disease systems are highly nonlinear, presenting substantial difficulties for both analysis and computation, which creates a continuous demand for efficient numerical methods that provide reliable solutions.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This study focused on the multiscale model characterising norovirus infection, comparing the multistage spectral relaxation method (MSRM) with the nonstandard finite difference method (NSFDM) in terms of convergence and accuracy.
analysis.methods: Both schemes were validated against an adaptive ODE45 scheme in MATLAB2025a, with parameter sensitivity analysis varying βH, δH, αh, μV, μH, and including semi-log error graphs, convergence rate visuals, and CPU performance benchmarks.
analysis.main_results: The numerical outcomes indicate that MSRM achieves better accuracy with relative L2 errors ranging from 10−9 to 10−7 for Δτ≤0.10 and Nch=8, while NSFDM provides solid first-order accuracy with L2 errors around 10−4, ensuring strict unconditional positivity and stability across all tested step sizes from h=0.01 to 2.0.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret that MSRM is the preferred method for high-fidelity applications due to its better accuracy for between-host variables, despite costing about 24 times more per run, while NSFDM is optimal for quick parameter sweeps and long simulations requiring guaranteed positivity.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: This study provides valuable insights for computational modeling of norovirus infection systems, offering guidance on selecting appropriate numerical methods based on the trade-offs between accuracy, computational cost, and stability for different research applications.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence strength is high as the study includes comprehensive validation against a reference solver and detailed performance comparisons, though the computational cost of MSRM may limit its practicality for large-scale simulations.

analysis.summary_en: This study addresses the challenge of solving highly nonlinear multiscale models for norovirus infection by comparing two numerical methods: the multistage spectral relaxation method (MSRM) and the nonstandard finite difference method (NSFDM). Validated against MATLAB's ODE45 solver, MSRM demonstrated superior accuracy with L2 errors ranging from 10−9 to 10−7, while NSFDM provided reliable first-order accuracy with errors around 10−4 and guaranteed positivity. Although MSRM costs 24 times more per run, it is preferred for high-fidelity applications, whereas NSFDM is better suited for quick parameter sweeps and long simulations. The study includes parameter sensitivity analysis and performance benchmarks, offering valuable guidance for computational modeling of norovirus systems.

The findings provide a foundation for developing next-generation vaccines and antiviral therapies against this globally significant pathogen, which infects 600-700 million people annually.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Human norovirus (HuNoV) is a major cause of acute viral gastroenteritis. Although it can be replicated in vitro using human intestinal enteroids (HIEs), generating high-titer viral laboratory stocks remains challenging due to low infection and passage efficiencies.
analysis.study_design_and_population: Here, we evaluated the effect of their inhibitors, ruxolitinib-a Janus kinase (JAK) 1/JAK2 inhibitor-and TAK-779-a C-X-C motif chemokine receptor 3 (CXCR3)/C-C motif chemokine receptor (CCR) 5/CCR2 antagonist-on HuNoV replication in wild-type jejunal HIEs.
analysis.methods: Interferon response and chemokine signaling may be key host pathways that restrict efficient HuNoV replication.
analysis.main_results: TAK-779 increased GII.17 HuNoV replication by 2.3- and 6.0-fold at 48 and 96 h postinfection (hpi), respectively, compared with the DMSO-treated control.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: In contrast, ruxolitinib alone did not affect viral replication.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: Notably, simultaneous treatment with these compounds further enhanced GII.17 replication by 6.0- and 10.7-fold at 48 and 96 hpi, respectively, which enabled serial passaging.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: These findings imply that the simultaneous suppression of these pathways potentially benefits GII.17 HuNoV replication.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the impact of ruxolitinib and TAK-779 on GII.17 human norovirus (HuNoV) replication in human intestinal enteroids (HIEs). The research aimed to address the challenge of generating high-titer viral stocks due to low replication efficiency. The results showed that TAK-779 significantly increased viral replication at 48 and 96 hpi, while ruxolitinib alone had no effect. Simultaneous treatment with both compounds led to a further enhancement, enabling serial passaging. These findings suggest that targeting interferon response and chemokine signaling pathways could improve HuNoV replication in vitro. The study provides insights into potential therapeutic strategies for norovirus infections but has limited implications for broader applications due to its focus on a specific viral genotype and in vitro model.

analysis.research_question_and_background: This study aimed to develop an early-warning framework for forecasting oyster norovirus outbreaks by leveraging environmental predictors. The research addresses the challenge of understanding and predicting the spread of norovirus in oyster populations, which is critical for public health and food safety.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study employed three artificial intelligence-based models - XGBoost, Random Forest (RF), and Deep Artificial Neural Network (DANN) - to forecast oyster norovirus outbreaks with a 2-day lead time. These models were constructed and tested using epidemiological and environmental data from three distinct coastal countries.
analysis.methods: The XGBoost model was selected for its superior performance, incorporating five environmental predictors (solar radiation, water temperature, gage height, precipitation, and salinity) along with their time-lags ranging from 2-30 days. These variables were identified using Pearson correlation and Gini index analyses.
analysis.main_results: The study found that solar radiation and water temperature are the two most important predictors of oyster norovirus outbreaks. Additionally, it revealed a strong long-range dependence of outbreaks on antecedent marine environmental conditions up to 30 days prior.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The novel features of the XGBoost model, including its use of environmental predictors and time-lagged data, provide an effective early-warning framework for managing oyster norovirus outbreaks.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings can inform proactive management strategies for oyster norovirus outbreaks, enhancing surveillance and risk assessment efforts in coastal regions.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study's evidence is based on data from three coastal countries, which may limit generalisability. However, the high accuracy of the XGBoost model suggests strong predictive performance.

analysis.summary_en: This study presents three artificial intelligence-based models - XGBoost, Random Forest (RF), and Deep Artificial Neural Network (DANN) - for forecasting oyster norovirus outbreaks with a 2-day lead time. The XGBoost model, which incorporates environmental predictors such as solar radiation and water temperature, demonstrated the highest accuracy. The research identifies solar radiation and water temperature as the most significant factors influencing outbreaks and highlights the long-range dependence of these outbreaks on antecedent marine environmental conditions up to 30 days prior. The findings suggest that the XGBoost model can serve as an effective early-warning framework for managing norovirus outbreaks in oyster populations. While the study's data are limited to three coastal countries, the high accuracy of the model indicates strong evidence for its predictive capabilities. These results have implications for improving surveillance and risk assessment strategies in coastal regions to mitigate the public health risks associated with norovirus contamination in oysters.

analysis.summary_en: This study conducted a phylogenetic analysis and examined clinical characteristics of sporadic norovirus diarrhea in adult outpatients in Beijing, China, during 2023–2024. It aimed to understand the molecular epidemiology of viral diarrhea and the role of norovirus in causing gastroenteritis. The research involved testing fecal samples using real-time RT-PCR and PCR for five enteric viruses, including norovirus, and performing genotyping and whole-genome sequencing on positive cases. Results showed that norovirus was the most prevalent pathogen, detected in 27.7% of patients, with GII.7[P7] strains showing close relatedness to 2024 strains from South Korea and Russia. The authors concluded that norovirus remains the leading cause of adult viral diarrhea in post-pandemic Beijing, with multiple genotypes co-circulating. The study's findings suggest the need for continued surveillance and updated diagnostic methods to address the ongoing evolution and transmission potential of non-GII.4 norovirus genotypes. However, the study's single-center design may limit its generalizability, and the evidence is considered moderate.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Diarrhea remains a leading cause of child morbidity and mortality. Improved and ongoing estimates of the etiology of hospitalized pediatric diarrhea in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs) are needed to help prioritize and evaluate the use of existing and upcoming vaccines and interventions.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The Global Pediatric Diarrhea Surveillance (GPDS) network is a World Health Organization (WHO)-coordinated public health surveillance network investigating the etiology of hospitalized diarrhea among children aged <5 years in LMICs. The GPDS network enrolls children hospitalized with diarrhea at 38 sentinel surveillance sites in 31 LMICs. During 2017-2022, the GPDS network enrolled 70,750 children aged <5 years hospitalized with diarrhea, of which 16,458 (23.3%) were randomly selected for qPCR testing.
analysis.methods: Randomly selected stool specimens were tested by TaqMan Array Card quantitative reverse-transcription polymerase chain reaction (qPCR) for 16 pathogens associated with diarrhea.
analysis.main_results: The most prevalent pathogen detected, regardless of quantity or modeled etiologic attribution, was rotavirus (weighted prevalence 30.4%), followed by adenovirus 40/41 (19.1%), norovirus (17.9%), Shigella (14.1%), and Campylobacter jejuni/coli (8.6%). Overall, in 2017-2022, rotavirus was the leading etiology globally (AF 32.5%; 95% Confidence Interval (CI): 27.4, 37.6), followed by Shigella (9.8%; 8.4, 11.3), adenovirus 40/41 (8.6%; 6.3, 10.8) and norovirus (6.7%; 5.6, 7.7). Norovirus AF increased slightly from 6.2% (4.7, 7.7) in 2017-2018 to 7.3% (5.0, 9.2) in 2021-2022. Global Shigella burden remained stable, and adenovirus 40/41 demonstrated significant volatility, peaking globally in 2019-2020 (11.9%; 5.9, 17.5).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: Despite the widespread use of rotavirus vaccines, rotavirus remained the leading cause of severe diarrhea among children aged <5 years in LMICs globally. However, the proportion of pediatric diarrhea attributable to rotavirus consistently declined from 2017-2018 to 2021-2022, and there were notable differences in the distribution of diarrheal etiologies between regions and across time periods.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: Improving the efficacy and coverage of rotavirus vaccination and prioritizing interventions against other enteric pathogens could further reduce diarrhea morbidity and mortality.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The supplied evidence does not report specific limitations of the study.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the etiology of hospitalized diarrhea in children under 5 years of age in 31 low- and middle-income countries (LMICs) through the Global Pediatric Diarrhea Surveillance (GPDS) network. The research highlights that norovirus was the second most prevalent pathogen, with an attributable fraction (AF) of 6.7% (5.6, 7.7) globally in 2017-2022. The study found that rotavirus, despite vaccine introduction, remained the leading cause of severe diarrhea, with its AF declining over time. The findings suggest that while rotavirus vaccines have had an impact, other pathogens like norovirus and Shigella also contribute significantly to the burden of disease. These results emphasize the need for improved vaccination coverage and targeted interventions against multiple enteric pathogens to reduce diarrhea-related morbidity and mortality in children. The study's evidence is based on qPCR testing of stool specimens from 70,750 children, with 16,458 randomly selected for analysis. The evidence strength is moderate, as the study is observational and relies on surveillance data.

Major evidence gaps include the absence of standardized norovirus monitoring tools and scalable decontamination approaches in produce environments.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The San Diego/Tijuana coastal region faces persistent water quality challenges due to untreated wastewater discharges, creating a public health need for timely risk forecasts for beachgoers. Existing same-day Enterococcus measurements provide limited decision-making value without predictive capacity.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study describes the development and evaluation of the Pathogen Forecast Model (PFM) V1.0, which generates daily 5-day forecasts of swimmer illness risk along 30 km of shoreline via a web dashboard. The model integrates hydrodynamic inputs including forecasted waves, winds, offshore currents, and Tijuana River flow.
analysis.methods: PFM uses a hydrodynamic model with forecasted environmental drivers to simulate tracer concentrations representing untreated wastewater decay modeled after Norovirus. Forecast accuracy was assessed by comparing modeled tracer concentrations with observed Enterococcus levels over 13 km of shoreline.
analysis.main_results: PFM accurately forecasts tides and waves and moderately predicts depth-averaged shelf currents. Forecasted tracer concentrations and observed Enterococcus levels showed moderate log-correlation (≈0.5) for day-1 and day-5 forecasts over 13 km of shoreline. The power-law relationship between tracer and Enterococcus had an exponent of ≈0.5.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The study reports that PFM is the first forecast model resolving estuarine, surfzone, and shelf regions, addressing a gap in spatially explicit risk prediction. The model's classification of advisory exceedances using a cutoff tracer concentration achieved nearly 80% raw accuracy with high sensitivity and lower specificity.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: PFM provides a public health tool for proactive beach advisories by forecasting pathogen risk up to five days in advance, potentially reducing swimmer illness through timely risk communication. The model's integration of hydrodynamic and tracer decay parameters offers a mechanistic basis for risk estimation.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence strength is moderate due to reliance on a proxy tracer for Norovirus and moderate correlation with observed Enterococcus, which may not fully capture viral behavior. The model's specificity for advisory exceedances was lower than sensitivity, indicating potential overestimation of risk in some contexts.

analysis.summary_en: The Pathogen Forecast Model (PFM) V1.0 was developed to address persistent water quality issues in the San Diego/Tijuana coastal region by providing daily 5-day forecasts of swimmer illness risk along 30 km of shoreline. Using a hydrodynamic model driven by forecasted waves, winds, offshore currents, and Tijuana River flow, PFM simulates tracer concentrations representing untreated wastewater decay modeled after Norovirus. The model accurately forecasts tides and waves and moderately predicts shelf currents, with forecasted tracer concentrations showing moderate log-correlation (≈0.5) with observed Enterococcus levels over 13 km of shoreline. The power-law relationship between tracer and Enterococcus had an exponent of ≈0.5, suggesting differential decay rates. PFM classified advisory exceedances with nearly 80% raw accuracy, high sensitivity, and lower specificity. As the first model resolving estuarine, surfzone, and shelf regions, PFM offers a mechanistic tool for proactive public health advisories, though its reliance on a proxy tracer and moderate correlation with observed data limit confidence in direct Norovirus risk estimation.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to evaluate evidence on human intestinal mucosa development, glycan expression from the fetal stage through childhood, and susceptibility to enteric viral infections from the fetal stage through childhood. The background highlights that human intestinal epithelial maturation involves cellular differentiation, structural maturation, and functional development, which are critical for understanding host-pathogen interactions.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A scoping review was conducted across Pubmed, Scopus, Cochrane Library, Embase, and Scielo for studies between 2010 and 2025. Information was extracted from original articles, observational studies, cohort studies, outbreak investigations, case-control studies, and experimental studies. The review focused on children up to 5 years of age.
analysis.methods: Following the PRISMA-ScR guidelines, the scoping review included studies published between 2010 and 2025. Excel spreadsheets were used for article accounting, and the analysis of 24 studies identified an ontogenetic pattern of viral susceptibility.
analysis.main_results: An early stage (<6 months) characterized by predominantly asymptomatic infections and a strong maternal influence is followed by a critical window of clinical vulnerability between 6 and 18 months. This period coincides with weaning and waning passive protection, exhibiting peak strong maternal influence and asymptomatic infections caused by secretor-dependent dominant genotypes (Norovirus GII.4, Rotavirus P[8]). Furthermore, glycocalyx maturation modulates live vaccine performance.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted the findings as evidence that enteric virus susceptibility is a dynamic developmental process driven by the transition from passive maternal protection to endogenous mucosal glycosylation. They emphasized that clinical disease depends on specific developmental time windows rather than fixed genetic status, highlighting the need for age-tailored immunization strategies beyond static binary secretor/non-secretor models.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings can inform the development of age-tailored immunization strategies for enteric viral infections, particularly for Norovirus GII.4 and Rotavirus P[8], by highlighting the importance of developmental time windows in susceptibility and vaccine performance.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its reliance on published literature up to 2025 and the potential for heterogeneity among the included studies. The evidence strength is moderate, as the findings are based on a scoping review of 24 studies rather than a randomized controlled trial or longitudinal study.

analysis.summary_en: This scoping review explores the ontogeny of human intestinal glycans and its impact on susceptibility to enteric viral infections in children up to 5 years of age. The study aimed to evaluate evidence on mucosal development, glycan expression, and viral susceptibility across the fetal to childhood stages. Using PRISMA-ScR guidelines, 24 studies were analyzed, revealing an ontogenetic pattern of susceptibility, with an early stage of predominantly asymptomatic infections and a critical window of clinical vulnerability between 6 and 18 months. This period coincides with weaning and waning maternal protection, marked by infections from secretor-dependent genotypes such as Norovirus GII.4 and Rotavirus P[8]. The authors interpret these findings as evidence of a dynamic developmental process in enteric virus susceptibility, emphasizing the need for age-specific immunization strategies. The study's implications suggest that understanding developmental time windows could improve surveillance, diagnosis, and vaccine development for enteric viral infections. However, the evidence is moderate due to the scoping review design and potential study heterogeneity.

analysis.scope_and_question: The review examines human norovirus (HuNoV), a non-enveloped, positive-sense RNA virus, as the leading cause of acute viral gastroenteritis globally, focusing on its molecular targets, antiviral therapeutics, and vaccine development strategies within human populations. The central question addresses the unmet need for effective antiviral drugs and vaccines despite substantial progress in understanding HuNoV molecular biology and replication mechanisms.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: This narrative review synthesizes evidence on HuNoV antiviral strategies without reporting databases, search dates, eligibility criteria, or study counts. It relies on critical analysis of molecular mechanisms, immune evasion, and replication, emphasizing key antiviral targets and therapeutic development based on available literature.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The review concludes that historical limitations in experimental model systems and HuNoV's ability to evade host antiviral responses have hindered the development of effective antiviral strategies. Recent advances in in vitro culture systems, particularly human intestinal enteroids, and inhibitor screening platforms have improved antiviral candidate identification, while preclinical and early-stage clinical studies have demonstrated immunogenicity in vaccine development.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: Significant challenges remain, including antigenic diversity, strain-specific immunity, and the lack of established correlates of protection. The review highlights persistent gaps in understanding HuNoV immune evasion mechanisms and the need for improved correlates of protection to guide vaccine design and therapeutic development.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The review prioritizes the development of robust experimental model systems, such as human intestinal enteroids, to facilitate antiviral screening and mechanistic studies. It also emphasizes the need for research into antigenic diversity and strain-specific immunity to inform vaccine strategies and the identification of correlates of protection to guide therapeutic and preventive measures.

analysis.summary_en: This review critically analyzes human norovirus (HuNoV), a leading cause of acute viral gastroenteritis, focusing on antiviral targets, therapeutics, and vaccine development. HuNoV's non-enveloped, positive-sense RNA genome and extensive genetic diversity contribute to recurrent outbreaks and complicate antiviral and vaccine efforts. While recent advances in in vitro culture systems and inhibitor screening have improved antiviral candidate identification, effective licensed therapeutics remain limited. Vaccine development has shown immunogenicity in preclinical and early-stage clinical studies, but antigenic diversity, strain-specific immunity, and the absence of correlates of protection pose major challenges. The review underscores the need for improved experimental models and research into immune evasion mechanisms to guide future therapeutic and preventive strategies.

The findings suggest human-to-animal transmission may be more likely than the reverse, with viral uptake acting as a species barrier. This is the first ex vivo demonstration of human norovirus replication in pig tissue, underscoring the need for surveillance of animal reservoirs to assess zoonotic risk.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated water quality degradation during the unprecedented May 2024 flood in Porto Alegre, Brazil, using high-resolution spatial sampling across 92 sites during the flood peak. The study provides in situ, quantitative evidence of pathogen dissemination during extreme flooding and proposes a replicable framework for risk assessment and urban water management.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Norovirus is a leading cause of pediatric acute gastroenteritis, yet the rare GII.8[P8] genotype remains under-characterized due to limited whole-genome data.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A GII.8[P8] norovirus strain, Harbin-Nov-076-2022, was identified through routine pediatric acute gastroenteritis surveillance in Harbin, China.
analysis.methods: The strain was recovered from a stool sample of a 15-month-old female patient and sequenced on the DNBSEQ-T7 platform, followed by phylogenetic reconstruction, amino acid entropy profiling, selection pressure assessment, homology modeling of the capsid P protein, and B-cell epitope prediction.
analysis.main_results: The near-complete genome of Harbin-Nov-076-2022 is 7486 nt long with 53.81% GC content, assigned to the GII.8[P8] lineage and showing 97.52% nucleotide identity to the Thai 2018 strain GII/Hu/TH/2018/GII.8[P8]/B6213.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The study expands whole-genome evidence for GII.8[P8] in Northeast China and identifies localized sequence-associated variations in the P2 subdomain and HBGA-binding loops, alongside 59 predicted B-cell epitopes.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings provide regional genomic data to inform molecular surveillance, evolutionary assessment, and antigenic characterization of non-dominant norovirus genotypes.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence is limited by the single-strain analysis and absence of functional validation of predicted epitopes, warranting a moderate confidence assessment.

analysis.summary_en: This study characterized a rare norovirus GII.8[P8] strain, Harbin-Nov-076-2022, detected during pediatric acute gastroenteritis surveillance in Harbin, China. Whole-genome sequencing revealed a 7486 nt genome with 53.81% GC content and 97.52% nucleotide identity to a Thai 2018 reference. Phylogenetic assignment confirmed the GII.8[P8] lineage, while amino acid variability was highest in VP2 with three variable sites. Selection pressure analysis indicated purifying selection across the genome. Homology modeling predicted localized sequence-associated variations in the P2 subdomain and HBGA-binding loops, and 59 B-cell epitopes were predicted. The findings expand whole-genome evidence for this rare genotype and provide regional genomic data to support molecular surveillance, evolutionary assessment, and antigenic characterization of non-dominant norovirus genotypes.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Acute gastroenteritis (AGE) is a major public health concern in Africa, with noroviruses recognized as predominant viral etiological agents. However, their epidemiological impact remains underreported in the Republic of Congo, particularly in Brazzaville.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A descriptive cross-sectional study was conducted from June to November 2020 at the University Hospital Center of Brazzaville. Fifty children aged 28 days to 17 years presenting with AGE were enrolled, with eighty percent aged ≤5 years.
analysis.methods: Stool samples were analyzed using real-time reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR) to detect viral RNA and differentiate between GI and GII genogroups.
analysis.main_results: The overall prevalence of norovirus infection was 44%, with GII (73%) predominating over GI (18%). GI/GII co-infections were detected in 9% of cases. A significant association was observed between age and norovirus genogroup distribution (p = 0.03), with GII being more prevalent among children aged ≤5 years.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: Norovirus represents an important cause of pediatric AGE in Brazzaville. The study identified circulating genogroups and highlighted age-related distribution differences, contributing to local molecular epidemiology knowledge.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings support the integration of molecular diagnostic approaches into national surveillance programs and the strengthening of sanitation measures to improve prevention and control strategies for norovirus gastroenteritis.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study’s cross-sectional design and small sample size limit causal inference and generalizability. The evidence strength is assessed as moderate due to potential selection bias and lack of longitudinal follow-up.

analysis.summary_en: This study assessed the molecular epidemiology of human norovirus among children with acute gastroenteritis in Brazzaville, Republic of Congo. Using RT-PCR, it detected norovirus in 44% of 50 enrolled children, with GII genogroups predominating (73%) and a significant age-related distribution (p = 0.03). Co-infections were present in 9% of cases. The authors conclude norovirus is a major pediatric AGE pathogen locally and recommend integrating molecular diagnostics into surveillance and improving sanitation. Limitations include a small sample size, cross-sectional design, and potential selection bias, warranting cautious interpretation.

analysis.research_and_practice_implications: Recent modelling studies have shown that early diagnosis and isolation of symptomatic individuals substantially reduce secondary transmission, yet routine genomic surveillance is rarely implemented onboard.

The findings suggest that strengthening surveillance systems and infection control protocols could improve global preparedness for norovirus outbreaks associated with international travel.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Norovirus (NoV) is a major cause of acute gastroenteritis in children, but pathogen-confirmed data in neonates remain limited, particularly regarding clinical differences associated with gastrointestinal bleeding.
analysis.study_design_and_population: We conducted a single-center retrospective observational study of neonates younger than 28 days who were hospitalized at the Children's Hospital of Soochow University between December 31, 2024 and December 31, 2025, had positive stool NoV antigen results, and underwent confirmatory nucleic acid testing.
analysis.methods: After excluding clinically identifiable alternative causes of gastrointestinal bleeding, patients were classified into hemorrhagic and non-hemorrhagic groups. Baseline characteristics, clinical manifestations, comorbidities, and laboratory findings obtained within 24 h after admission were compared between groups. Laboratory variables showing significant between-group differences were entered into a multivariable logistic regression model.
analysis.main_results: A total of 139 neonates were included, comprising 52 in the hemorrhagic group and 87 in the non-hemorrhagic group. Among the hemorrhagic cases, 49 had overt gastrointestinal bleeding and three had isolated fecal occult blood positivity.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The hemorrhagic group had a higher frequency of diarrhea and a lower frequency of jaundice. Hemoglobin, total bilirubin, indirect bilirubin, aspartate aminotransferase, the aspartate aminotransferase/alanine aminotransferase ratio, pH-corrected venous ionized calcium, chloride, and lactate were lower in the hemorrhagic group, whereas blood base excess was higher.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that specific clinical and laboratory features may be associated with gastrointestinal bleeding in neonates with norovirus gastroenteritis, which could inform targeted surveillance and management strategies.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The association with lower ionized calcium should be interpreted cautiously because of the retrospective design and potential residual confounding.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated clinical characteristics associated with gastrointestinal bleeding in neonates with laboratory-confirmed norovirus gastroenteritis. A single-center retrospective observational study was conducted on 139 neonates hospitalized between December 31, 2024, and December 31, 2025, at the Children's Hospital of Soochow University. Neonates were classified into hemorrhagic and non-hemorrhagic groups after excluding alternative causes of bleeding. Baseline characteristics, clinical manifestations, comorbidities, and laboratory findings were compared between groups. The hemorrhagic group showed a higher frequency of diarrhea and lower levels of hemoglobin, total bilirubin, and ionized calcium, along with higher blood base excess. A multivariable logistic regression model found that each 0.1 mmol/L increase in ionized calcium was associated with lower odds of the hemorrhagic phenotype. The study highlights potential clinical and laboratory markers for gastrointestinal bleeding in neonates with norovirus infection, which could aid in targeted surveillance and management. However, the retrospective design and potential residual confounding limit the strength of the findings.

analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study's evidence is limited to synthetic RNA standards and 28 wastewater samples, which may affect generalizability. analysis.summary_en: This study introduces a contamination-free lateral flow platform for detecting norovirus and rotavirus in wastewater. The platform combines recombinase polymerase amplification with CRISPR-associated protein 13a and gold nanoparticle-based detection. The results showed no cross-reactivity with non-target viruses and 14 positive detections across 56 tests, comparable to quantitative polymerase chain reaction. The findings highlight the platform's potential for enhancing wastewater-based epidemiology and public health surveillance. However, the study's limited sample size and reliance on synthetic standards may affect generalizability, resulting in moderate confidence in the results.

analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its reliance on sera from healthy adults, which may not fully represent immune responses in all populations. The evidence is moderate, as it is based on comparative analysis of strains rather than direct clinical outcomes.

However, the study is limited by its use of sera from healthy adults and the absence of direct clinical outcomes, resulting in moderate evidence strength.

analysis.scope_and_question: Common variable immunodeficiency (CVID), the most prevalent symptomatic primary antibody deficiency (∼1:25,000), in its symptomatic spectrum reaches way beyond intractable, chronic, and recurrent infections. Noninfectious enteropathy (CVID-E)—affecting 15–30% of patients—has emerged as a pivotal manifestation of the natural disease trajectory, with approximately 11-fold increased mortality risk.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: USIDNET registry analysis (n = 1,415) confirmed that CVID-E patients exhibit significantly lower performance status, higher rates of concomitant autoimmunity (30.7%), granulomatous disease, and even malignancy. Multicenter randomized controlled trials and precision therapeutics are urgently needed to supersede the current empirical interventions with a fully evidence-based approach.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: CVID-E is pathologically determined by villous atrophy, absent mucosal plasma cells, and abundant CD8+ T cell infiltration—yielding the phenotype that often mimics celiac disease. There are three pathogenic determinants that have been elucidated so far. First, almost absent mucosal IgA is permeating and facilitating gut pathogen expansion. With this process, gut membrane lipid metabolism is shifted toward inflammatory cascades, which may render an inflammatory bowel disease (IBD)-like phenotype. Second, a mixed and specific type I/III and type II interferon release drives CD8+ T cell cytotoxicity and macrophage recruitment, producing a graft-versus-host-like mucosal damage pattern yielding apparent villous injury.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: Immunoglobulin replacement does not mitigate symptoms of enteropathy, and although corticosteroids restore architecture, they impose prohibitive infectious risk. Although TNF-α blockers and thiopurines achieved complete remission in select patient cohorts, overall therapeutic response was unsatisfying. Treatment is largely empirical with limited evidence-based data.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: Molecular medical tactics—employing JAK inhibitors targeting the interferon-specific pathways, namely abatacept for CTLA-4-related dysregulation—represent the most promising tool. CVID-E is a complicated disorder because it stands at the very intersection of immunodeficiency, immune dysregulation, and mucosal pathology where these determinants encompass collapsed humoral defense, gut dysbiosis, and unbalanced interferon-driven epithelial necrosis converge.

analysis.summary_en: This review explores the role of norovirus in the pathogenesis of CVID-E, a noninfectious enteropathy associated with common variable immunodeficiency (CVID). CVID-E is characterized by villous atrophy, absent mucosal plasma cells, and CD8+ T cell infiltration, often mimicking celiac disease. The review highlights three pathogenic determinants: mucosal IgA deficiency leading to gut pathogen expansion, interferon-driven immune responses causing mucosal damage, and chronic norovirus infection exacerbating these pathways. Despite the potential of JAK inhibitors and abatacept, current treatments remain empirical with limited evidence-based data. The review emphasizes the need for multicenter randomized controlled trials and precision therapeutics to address the complexities of CVID-E, which involves immunodeficiency, immune dysregulation, and mucosal pathology.

analysis.brief_en: A gastrointestinal illness outbreak on the National Geographic Sea Bird cruise ship affected eight guests and five crew members during its July 15 voyage, according to the CDC. The symptoms included abdominal cramps, vomiting, and diarrhea, and this is the fourth such outbreak in less than two months. The cause of the illness remains unknown, though previous outbreaks on the same ship were linked to norovirus. In response, Lindblad Expeditions and the ship’s crew implemented enhanced cleaning and disinfection procedures, isolated affected individuals, and consulted with the Vessel Sanitation Program. The company also canceled three voyages scheduled for July 20, July 25, and July 30 to ensure additional sanitation measures. The CDC reported nine outbreaks of gastrointestinal illness on cruise ships this year, with five attributed to norovirus and two to E. coli, while the rest are still under investigation. The ship is currently en route to Ketchikan, Alaska.

e0e9f36f22f08f828c6c0f8cb7229f0771351178.text: BioFire FilmArray 胃肠道面板上 诺如病毒 假阳性结果的分子表征

2fb7c9b123bbb114a81e366ebb03d62842673f43.text: 未标记:BioFire FilmArray Gastrointestinal Panel (BF-GIP) 等分子综合征组合因其快速周转时间和广泛的病原体覆盖范围而被广泛用于胃肠道疾病 诊断。最近,BF-GIP 证明 诺如病毒 假阳性检测率有所增加,促使 2024 年 2 月对超过 200 万次检测进行了 II 级召回,并导致过去 5 年报告的超过 25 万个假阳性 诺如病毒 结果的估计负担。我们从 2024 年 12 月到 2025 年 6 月检查了四家医院的 BF-GIP 诺如病毒 假阳性结果。在 BD MAX 肠道病毒检测组确认的 185 例 BF-GIP 诺如病毒 阳性结果中,各个地点的假发现率在 31% 到 74% 之间,其中在专门的癌症护理医院中出现的假发现率最高。BF-GIP 袋 (n = 42) 的深度测序证实了 Noro-1 检测是脱靶扩增的主要来源,识别出 78 种脱靶物种(主要是共生粪便细菌),而 Noro-2 检测仅识别出两种脱靶物种。从假阳性和真阴性袋中均发现了通过 Noro-1 检测扩增的脱靶物种,这表明没有单一物种导致了假阳性结果。脱靶位点的部分引物互补性和可接受范围内的扩增子 Tm 值支持肠道微生物群的错误引发是根本原因。对于两种检测,假阳性袋的交叉点值均显着高于真阳性袋(Noro-1:26.6 vs 11.1,P = 0.013;Noro-2:30.0 vs 13.1,P < 0.001),与低水平脱靶扩增一致。这些发现凸显了 Noro-1 检测的高错误发现率,识别了引发错误的细菌种类,并证明需要重新设计该检测以确保可靠的检测和改善患者护理。重要性:综合征分子组彻底改变了胃肠道诊断。然而,最近的数据表明 诺如病毒 假阳性结果与 BioFire FilmArray Gastrointestinal Panel 相关。在这里,我们调查了与该检测的 2024 年 II 级召回相关的重大诊断失败,揭示了在某些临床环境中 诺如病毒 错误发现率高达 74%。通过对 FilmArray 袋中的扩增子进行深度测序,我们发现 Noro-1 检测与粪便微生物组核酸存在广泛的交叉反应。从 42 个临床袋的 78 种细菌中检测到脱靶 Noro-1 扩增子。对于每袋读取计数最高的 16 个物种,扩增子映射到具有部分引物重叠的离散基因组位点,与错误引发一致。这些离散位点的识别,加上多项研究报告的反复高错误发现率,使得临床迫切需要重新设计该检测方法。我们的工作还强调了对严格的上市后 监测 的持续需求以及深度测序在诊断分析失败故障排除中的实用性。

23ea2e4e7a5814367913487d342deb142a3b0aff.text: BioFire FilmArray Gastrointestinal Panel 等分子综合征组合由于周转时间短和病原体覆盖范围广而被广泛用于胃肠道疾病 诊断,但最近的数据表明与该组合相关的 诺如病毒 存在显着的假阳性结果。

b006f1193dc5fd205a81b990b61ba5da2147677d.text: 我们检查了 2024 年 12 月至 2025 年 6 月期间四家医院的 BF-GIP 诺如病毒 的 患病率 假阳性情况。

84151c42c1e3082c0f1d6c941f50c9425e0e5007.text: BF-GIP 袋 (n = 42) 的深度测序证实了 Noro-1 检测是脱靶扩增的主要来源,识别出 78 种脱靶物种(主要是共生粪便细菌),而 Noro-2 检测仅识别出两种脱靶物种。

f5102dd964bd7eb3f12db7b993ee3beb93536b08.text: 在 BD MAX 肠道病毒检测组确认的 185 份 BF-GIP 诺如病毒 阳性结果中,不同地点的错误发现率在 31% 至 74% 之间,其中在专门的癌症护理医院中发现的错误率最高。

0f2c49738b14fe95e7d1df614dc624464a6e0d6f.text: 这些发现凸显了 Noro-1 检测的高错误发现率,识别了引发错误的细菌种类,并证明需要重新设计该检测以确保可靠的检测和改善患者护理。

8b0d14e8fb14f45179ddb1333f3220d74971680f.text: 具有部分引物重叠的离散基因座的识别,加上多项研究报告的反复高错误发现率,使得重新设计该检测方法成为临床上的当务之急,并强调了对严格的上市后 监测 的持续需求。

12858915417aadd3d19327524be0d80c82520470.text: 尽管该研究仅限于四家医院并且可能无法代表所有临床环境,但由于样本量大和验证性测试,证据强度很高。

3e366f658185209c62fa16478844afb1c5bf9aac.text: 粪便微生物群移植对抗 诺如病毒 感染:从机制到临床证据

ca2dedd449609e6487e5ccef4138b97454657391.text: 诺如病毒 (NoV) 是 急性胃肠炎 的全球领先事业。感染者在粪便中排出高浓度病毒,极低的感染剂量可以在家庭接触者中继发传播,从而扩大传播范围。目前,尚无批准的针对 NoV 感染的 抗病毒药物 特效疗法;因此,迫切需要开发新的治疗策略。粪便微生物群移植(FMT)通过移植健康供体的粪便微生物群来恢复肠道微生物群稳态,对于复发性艰难梭菌感染的疗效已得到充分证明。本文总结了 NoV 的生物学特性和感染机制、肠道菌群与 NoV 之间的双向相互作用,以及支持 FMT 在 NoV 感染中应用的临床证据。本综述还讨论了 FMT 在 NoV 感染中的潜在治疗机制,包括微生物群植入和结构重塑、肠粘膜屏障修复和免疫调节,并强调了其临床应用的关键考虑因素,如供体筛选、粪便准备和输送途径。现有证据表明,FMT 在治疗 NoV 感染方面可能具有良好的疗效和安全性,特别是对于免疫功能低下的患者。然而,目前的研究仅限于病例报告和小病例系列,缺乏大规模的随机对照试验。需要进一步的高质量研究和标准化方案来验证 FMT 的临床价值并促进其在 NoV 感染管理中的临床转化。

07bb4df1733441128a58078775a329df3d09d189.text: 本综述重点关注 急性胃肠炎 的全球主要病因 诺如病毒 (NoV),研究其生物学特征、感染机制以及粪便微生物群移植 (FMT) 作为治疗策略的潜力。核心问题是 FMT 能否有效治疗 NoV 感染,尤其是免疫功能低下的患者。

7d633227530de08a53dfb850a5000b76484033c9.text: 这是一篇叙述性综述,总结了 NoV 生物学、微生物群-病毒相互作用以及 FMT 临床应用的现有证据。该审查没有指定数据库、检索日期或资格标准,也没有报告荟萃分析或共识过程。

fed5773978b892aca1f93e5a2732d817b771e56b.text: 共识是,FMT 在治疗 NoV 感染方面可能具有良好的疗效和安全性,特别是对于免疫功能低下的患者。主要结论包括 FMT 的潜在治疗机制,例如微生物移植、粘膜屏障修复和免疫调节。

e084506a97b47ded72588640cc5b6ed0391a50b7.text: 目前的证据仅限于病例报告和小病例系列,缺乏大规模随机对照试验。需要标准化方案和高质量研究来验证 FMT 对 NoV 感染的临床价值。

f2cf4b3ce5cf0a5c3cfce8b634027d7fff3766fe.text: 需要进一步的高质量研究和标准化方案来验证 FMT 的临床价值并促进其临床转化。临床应用的关键考虑因素包括供体筛选、粪便准备和输送途径。

d6e6f472db43b256dc88e77905448c90f27ca3b6.text: 在大肠杆菌 ArcticExpress (DE3) 中高效生产可溶性全长 诺如病毒 VP1,具有诊断分析开发的潜力。

c7daf5f8413981f963a6fa7f3c617707d606a417.text: 摘要 人类 诺如病毒 (HuNoVs) 是非细菌性胃肠炎的主要病原体之一。病毒衣壳蛋白 VP1 是诊断的主要目标。虽然真核表达系统可以产生正确组装的 VP1,但它们的成本较高且复杂。大肠杆菌原核表达系统对于大规模表达具有吸引力;然而,VP1 在常规菌株 (BL21 (DE3)) 中经常聚集成不溶性包涵体。ArcticExpress (DE3) 菌株共表达嗜冷伴侣蛋白,以改善低温下的蛋白质折叠,从而提高难以表达靶标的可溶性产量。在这项研究中,我们证明了大肠杆菌ArcticExpress (DE3)在低温诱导下能够高产生产HuNoVs GII.4和GII.17的可溶性全长VP1。在BL21(DE3)中,上述抗原聚集成不溶性包涵体。使用 ArcticExpress(DE3),在测试的基因型中,VP1 产量被确定为大约 18–93 mg/L。在 BL21 (DE3) 中,蛋白质结果是基因型依赖性的:GII.4 只能通过不溶性级分处理来恢复,GII.17 在测试条件下仍然检测不到或仅以痕量水平存在。ArcticExpress 衍生的病毒抗原保留了抗原特性,并被交叉反应性抗 GII 抗体识别。据我们所知,这项研究提供的证据表明 ArcticExpress (DE3) 能够溶解生产适合下游免疫化学分析的全长 HuNoVs VP1。

acf0098c646c0fd743ef67256e2373cac45206da.text: 人类 诺如病毒 (HuNoV) 是非细菌性胃肠炎的主要原因,其衣壳蛋白 VP1 是关键的诊断靶点。该研究旨在开发一种使用原核表达系统生产可溶性全长 VP1 的经济有效的方法。

0f7b6fa7f4affc2ff39bb8c9736eae50ce2dc8a0.text: 该研究利用大肠杆菌ArcticExpress (DE3)菌株生产HuNoVs GII.4和GII.17基因型的可溶性VP1,并将其性能与传统的BL21 (DE3)菌株进行比较。

a9232cc9a78efdf50d7468ed4ba41376a28e6eef.text: 研究人员在 ArcticExpress (DE3) 中采用低温诱导来增强蛋白质折叠和可溶性 VP1 产量,然后使用交叉反应性抗 GII 抗体进行抗原特性验证。

e27e3f8d60c1c586c3aae2842faeda7b9ae0e814.text: ArcticExpress (DE3) 在测试的基因型中产生的可溶性 VP1 产量为 18–93 mg/L,而 BL21 (DE3) 则产生不溶性聚集体或检测不到的水平。ArcticExpress 衍生的 VP1 保留了抗原特性。

e70d5228f9be094922bd7d861ea087ab7c1cf5a4.text: 该研究表明,ArcticExpress (DE3) 能够高产地可溶性生产全长 HuNoVs VP1,适用于免疫化学分析,解决了传统表达系统的局限性。

d17bfb91527f2b3ca8f76ef3322b67f934e9799d.text: 该方法通过提供可扩展的、经济高效的可溶性 VP1 来源,提高 监测 和检测能力,促进了 诺如病毒 诊断测定的开发。

4b7d79560d464ee945dae22be17bbc1ea15d9f15.text: 证据来自于基因型有限的单一研究,但结果一致并直接支持结论,表明可信度中等。

99755484e400b1acc90a5ee7aa4b81f0e439a807.text: IgA 对于预防 诺如病毒 感染是必要且充分的 2258197

53f9e94ccfe02c51bdcf8175abd37105ae30acac.text: 我们使用一组经过基因和药理学修饰的小鼠来研究小鼠 诺如病毒 (MNV) 感染保护的相关性和细胞决定因素,该感染可作为 HNV 的遗传易处理模型。

26adcf6b6d3a150875ed22e99eef86c20a919a3e.text: 我们采用基因和药理学修饰的小鼠来研究 MNV 感染保护的相关性和细胞决定因素,重点关注 T 细胞依赖性 IgA 和 CD8+ T 细胞。

805d423362a0d0ef718df82b765996c4c1d29ad3.text: T细胞依赖性IgA对于控制小肠中的MNV复制是必需的,而CD8+ T细胞是可有可无的;IgA 浆细胞介导防止再次感染的保护,二聚体 IgA(而非单体)足以提供针对 MNV 感染的完全保护。

03ba6be5f7cd2d4e6ef56ae34b66f6bf441befe3.text: 我们的工作表明,粘膜 IgA 对于控制小鼠模型中的 诺如病毒 感染至关重要,为合理的 疫苗 设计和 HNV 免疫治疗提供了重要见解。

38296e4b4f72f1f2b95dd37f54c410bedc50f8ec.text: 这些发现强调了粘膜 IgA 在 诺如病毒 保护中的关键作用,为开发有效的 疫苗 和针对粘膜免疫而不是全身反应的免疫治疗药物提供了信息。

36d773824f06fd5625bf066f6445340c93feaf56.text: 该研究是在小鼠模型中进行的,该模型可能无法完全重现人类 诺如病毒 感染;然而,由于严格使用经过基因和药理学修饰的小鼠来建立因果关系,因此证据强度很高。

4d10a0cf395518fc0d50a38cece1541d89316295.text: 人类 诺如病毒 GII.3 衣壳的构象可塑性揭示了替代的 P 结构域相互作用网络

5f38380c7ea94b2b6963679d4c056c7d105f4edc.text: 人类 诺如病毒 (HuNoV) 是全球 急性胃肠炎 的主要原因,但目前尚无有效的 抗病毒药物 治疗方法。尽管在小鼠 诺如病毒 (MNV) 中已经报道了环境诱导的与感染性相关的衣壳构象变化,但在 HuNoV 中尚未证实类似的构象转换。在这项研究中,我们使用杆状病毒表达系统生成了 HuNoV GII.3 病毒样颗粒 (VLP),并通过冷冻电子显微镜单颗粒分析鉴定了在源自单一菌株的 VLP 制品中共存的两个不同的 T = 3 颗粒群。比较结构分析表明,这两种 T = 3 衣壳构象对应于突出 (P) 结构域的静止和上升状态。P 结构域的重排改变了相邻衣壳亚基之间的分子间相互作用,导致不同的衣壳表面结构。在静息状态下,分子间接触主要由 P2 亚结构域介导,P1 亚结构域的贡献有限。相比之下,上升态表现出向主要涉及 P1 子域的替代相互作用界面的转变。伴随这种构象转换的衣壳表面的改变可以影响与病毒 宿主 和抗体的生物学相关的分子间相互作用,如小鼠 诺如病毒 中所证明的。这些发现证明了 HuNoV 衣壳中以前未被识别的结构多态性,并提供了 HuNoV 中可能发生构象转换的证据。我们的结果为 诺如病毒 衣壳动力学提供了新的见解,并可能为未来基于结构的 疫苗 和 抗病毒药物 药物开发提供信息。

070857b7e1245d56afcdcdb3dae18406889cf6ac.text: 人类 诺如病毒 是一种主要的 急性胃肠炎 病原体,具有高基因型多样性、突变 和重组率。现有的监测其遗传变异的测序方法受到灵敏度低和污染风险的限制。这项研究通过增加核酸输入、简化文库制备和引入可部署的基于 USER 酶的污染预防系统,优化了我们之前建立的微目标混合捕获系统 (MT-Capture)。优化的方案在 7 小时内完成文库制备和捕获。与多重PCR测序相比,优化的MT-Capture避免了引物更新,捕获多种基因型并提高了兼容性,并更有效地检测低丰度样本。USER 酶可降解污染的扩增子,确保数据的真实性。MT-Capture-USER 系统为 诺如病毒 全 基因组 测序和流行病学 监测 提供快速、灵敏且抗污染的方法。

f4eeacea3ceffdf3d3bc5830cf2113447ccff9e9.text: 诺如病毒 是美国 急性胃肠炎 (AGE) 的主要原因,与大量医疗保健利用(包括住院风险)相关。潜在的医疗状况在多大程度上导致这种风险尚不清楚。

22fd95ce5f2180b714c00993186f3f21d4564f80.text: 尽管亚洲腹泻病负担相当大,但病因特异性模式的特征仍然不充分。本研究旨在对 1990 年至 2023 年亚洲地区腹泻疾病负担进行全面评估,重点关注对旅行者腹泻的影响。

b763bef1d4b8008734c8d258604360f65c1efdb8.text: 我们利用 2023 年全球疾病负担研究估计了 1990 年至 2023 年间亚洲(包括中亚、东亚、南亚、东南亚和高收入亚太地区)34 个国家的腹泻疾病负担。

f530454939e43fb47a5ed24cfe7ddb74189f4f1a.text: 该研究依赖于 2023 年全球疾病负担研究,该研究在某些地区和时间段的数据质量和完整性方面可能存在局限性。由于数据的综合性,证据强度中等,但 监测 和报告存在潜在偏差。

48224d415007d5529d0c6342d8b829dc3614b4a0.text: 塞内加尔 流行病学 为期 3 年的基于废水的 流行病学 研究

bfd730799e748dc1a53d880d30fc788c5cee5909.text: 未标记:诺如病毒 是全球 急性胃肠炎 的主要原因,因为它具有高传染性、广泛的 传播 以及缺乏 治疗 或 疫苗。在塞内加尔,没有进行常规社区级监测,大多数可用数据涉及其他肠道病毒,这在了解 诺如病毒 传播方面留下了空白。为了评估废水 监测 作为预警系统的潜力,我们利用 2020 年至 2023 年期间收集的临床和环境数据,结合统计和机器学习模型,分析了塞内加尔 诺如病毒 的时空循环,并比较了基因型和 监测 系统之间的有效繁殖数 R(t) 估计值。我们的数据表明,诺如病毒 GII 是研究期间的优势基因型。此外,废水收集地点之间的病毒载量存在很强的空间异质性,在几个废水收集地点观察到病毒滴度较高。有趣的是,环境环境中病毒载量的峰值经常先于报告的临床病例的增加。建模数据表明 诺如病毒 GII 比 GI 更持久地循环。我们的研究结果还强调了时间、人口和临床因素对废水中病毒载量的影响。有效繁殖数 R(t) 的比较证实了描述性数据,并强调了 诺如病毒 GII 更持久的循环,以及在临床数据变化之前检测到废水数据中 R(t) 的增加,强调了废水环境 监测 作为 诺如病毒 监测 早期预警工具系统的有用性。我们的研究值得注意,代表了基于废水的 流行病学 的首次全国应用,以监测塞内加尔不同地理和人口背景下的 流行病学 循环。重要性:诺如病毒 代表了全球主要的公共卫生问题,特别是在资源有限的低收入和中等收入国家,例如塞内加尔。监测废水中的 诺如病毒 对于早期检测 暴发 和追踪病毒 进化 至关重要,因为这些病毒在临床环境中经常被诊断不足。在本研究中,我们利用 4 年多收集的临床和环境数据,并将建模方法与流行病学参数估计相结合,报告了塞内加尔 诺如病毒 的时空循环。我们的研究提供了第一个关于应用基于废水的 流行病学 来监测塞内加尔不同地理和人口背景下的 流行病学 的全国数据。我们的数据提供了一种主动且经济高效的方法来监测公共卫生趋势并确定人群中是否存在 诺如病毒,从而为社区传播提供早期预警系统。在缺乏常规临床 监测 的情况下,该方法可用于监测塞内加尔的其他公共卫生问题。

1214cf0a382c67ee211b2ea082abad812f47fe36.text: 诺如病毒 因其高传染性、广泛的 传播 以及 治疗 或 疫苗 的缺乏而成为全球范围内 急性胃肠炎 的主要原因。在塞内加尔,没有进行常规社区级监测,大多数可用数据涉及其他肠道病毒,这在了解 诺如病毒 传播方面留下了空白。

256a3dd371da1c23ffed2530e2eb5f0d03dded73.text: 病原体预测模型版本 1.0:圣地亚哥/蒂华纳地区基于流程的五天海滩咨询预测系统。

70cb30aa19b67d4a0ebf18bed6454bf19049a5f0.text: 由于未经处理的废水源,圣地亚哥/蒂华纳(美国/墨西哥)沿海地区存在严重的水质问题。定期 ddPCR 肠球菌采样可为海滩游客提供当天的水质信息,但不提供决策预测。我们描述了病原体预测模型 (PFM) V1.0,在网络仪表板上提供 30 公里海岸线上游泳者疾病风险的每日 5 天预测。PFM 基于水动力模型,使用预测的波浪、风、离岸流和蒂华纳河流量作为输入。PFM 可以准确地预测潮汐和波浪,并且可以较好地预测深度平均陆架流。建模的未处理废水浓度示踪剂 C 以代表 诺如病毒 的恒定衰减率演变。对于第 1 天和第 -5 天的预测,超过 13 公里的海岸线,预测的 C 和观察到的肠球菌 E 具有中等对数相关性 (≈0.5)。C 和 E 幂律关系的指数约为 0.5,这可能表明示踪剂的衰变速度比肠球菌 DNA 慢 2 倍,以及其他可能的解释。使用截断值 C = 10-5,PFM 对咨询超标进行分类,原始准确度接近 80%,灵敏度高,特异性较低。这是第一个解析河口、海浪带和陆架区域的预测模型。PFM 是一种有用的公共卫生工具,并且正在不断改进。

a64aebe91f53886716d342e95bab233e19915b48.text: 由于未经处理的废水源,圣地亚哥/蒂华纳沿海地区面临着严重的水质问题,因此需要一个游泳者疾病风险预测系统。

45e2343ef14c572f3c5124c6e78c17180b9660f0.text: 该研究开发了病原体预测模型 (PFM) V1.0,该模型每天对圣地亚哥/蒂华纳地区 30 公里海岸线的游泳者疾病风险进行 5 天预测。

29bb28bc147de3674f229e7f9fe83fc50051b15f.text: PFM 基于水动力模型,使用预测的波浪、风、离岸流和蒂华纳河流量作为输入,并使用代表 诺如病毒 衰减的建模示踪剂浓度。

8d49cc9ce790a2fb971ee04b9eb2903e73291be1.text: PFM 准确预测潮汐和波浪,适度预测陆架流,并在第 1 天和第 -5 天的预测中显示建模示踪剂 C 和观察到的肠球菌 E 之间的中等对数相关性 (≈0.5)。

88d37954d001e4de1880eeb160934334d729f426.text: 继针对轮状病毒 A (RVA) 的 疫苗接种 广泛传播后,诺如病毒 (NoV) 已成为 急性胃肠炎 (AGE) 的主要原因。然而,有关印度 NoV 的临床特征和分子 流行病学 的数据仍然有限。对 2013 年 4 月至 2023 年 5 月期间从印度马哈拉施特拉邦和古吉拉特邦两个城市收集的住院散发 AGE 病例的总共 1637 份粪便样本进行了 NoV 筛查。阳性样本通过分子基因分型进行表征。在 149 例(9.1%)病例中检测到 NoV,其中 123 例(82.5%)感染发生在 2 岁以下儿童中。大多数患者 103 (69.1%) 患有严重或非常严重的疾病,22.8% 患有混合病毒感染,主要是 RVA。基因分型鉴定出 11 种 VP1 基因型、9 种 RdRp P 型和大约 30 种基因型组合,显示出巨大的遗传多样性。GII.4 (n = 66) 和 GII.P16 (n = 67) 是主要变异,与不太常见的基因型相比,与更严重的疾病相关。经过验证的 qRT-PCR 检测显示,区域菌株的灵敏度和特异性 > 97%,从而实现快速、准确的 诊断。印度儿童中传播的 NoV 的广泛遗传多样性凸显了在未来 疫苗 开发中增强分子 监测、改进诊断以及考虑当地流行基因型的需要。

d3afa462ad85a071f40645a01a078bfc615c8da1.text: 人类 诺如病毒 (HuNoV) 是全球病毒性胃肠炎最常见的原因,导致散发病例和 暴发。感染野生和家养动物(包括猪和狗)的 诺如病毒 与人类 诺如病毒 有遗传相关性,增加了跨物种 传播 的可能性。为了研究 诺如病毒 跨越物种障碍的潜力,我们使用了猪、犬和禽类精密切割的肠道切片。我们发现,人 诺如病毒 病毒样颗粒 (VLP) 与猪和狗的肠道组织结合,并分别以与猪和犬 诺如病毒 相似的效率被吸收。相反,在鸡组织中没有检测到人、猪或犬诺如病毒的结合或内化。我们进一步表明,人 诺如病毒 在猪肠道组织中复制。相比之下,虽然动物 诺如病毒 附着在人类肠道细胞上,但细胞内的摄取受到限制。这表明人与动物之间的 传播 比动物与人之间的 传播 更有可能,并且病毒摄取可能存在物种障碍。
